rgba-to-hex-converter.quickAnswer: RGBA becomes HEX by writing each channel as two hex digits; alpha 0-1 is scaled to a 0-255 byte first. rgba(255, 87, 51, 0.5) converts to #FF573380: alpha 0.5 x 255 = 127.5, rounded to 128, which is 80 in hex. With alpha 1, the alpha byte is dropped and you get the plain 6-digit #FF5733.
keyFacts: 8-digit HEX is #RRGGBBAA: the last two digits are the alpha byte.
Alpha 0 = fully transparent, alpha 1 = fully opaque; 0.5 = half transparent.
The alpha byte = round(alpha x 255): 0.5 becomes 128, which is 80 in hex.
6-digit HEX has no alpha information - it always means fully opaque.
8-digit HEX works in all modern browsers in CSS color properties.

rgba-to-hex-converter.formula:
HEX = hex(R) + hex(G) + hex(B) + hex(round(A x 255)).
Example: rgba(255, 87, 51, 0.5):
R: 255 -> FF | G: 87 -> 57 | B: 51 -> 33
A: 0.5 x 255 = 127.5 -> 128 -> 80
Result: #FF573380 (8-digit) or #FF5733 (6-digit, alpha dropped).
rgba-to-hex-converter.workedExample:
rgba(255, 87, 51, 0.5):
1. Convert each channel: 255 = FF, 87 = 57, 51 = 33.

4. Join: #FF573380 - orange-red at half transparency.
5. Drop the alpha for the 6-digit form: #FF5733.

faqs.a: It is the standard 6-digit HEX plus two digits for alpha: #RRGGBBAA. #FF573380 is the same orange-red at 50% opacity. All modern browsers support it in CSS.

faqs.q: Why does alpha 0.5 become 80 in hex?
faqs.a: Alpha is stored as one byte (0-255). 0.5 x 255 = 127.5, rounded to 128. In hexadecimal, 128 is 80 (8 x 16 + 0).

faqs.q: When should I use 6-digit instead of 8-digit?
faqs.a: Use 6-digit when the color is fully opaque (alpha 1) - it is shorter and universally supported. Use 8-digit whenever transparency matters.
Yes, exactly. They describe the identical color and transparency; only the notation differs.

faqs.q: Can I convert the other way, HEX to RGBA?
faqs.a: Read the pairs: #FF573380 splits into FF=255, 57=87, 33=51, 80=128, and 128/255 = 0.5 alpha - so rgba(255, 87, 51, 0.5).

faqs.q: Does alpha 0 make the color invisible?
faqs.a: Yes - alpha 0 means fully transparent. The HEX still describes a color (#FF573300), but nothing of it is painted.
